item.text: {"schema":"voice-draft-source/2","kind":"draft","paragraphs":[{"sentences":[{"text":"A device is not fully owned when its maker can disable features after sale.","basis":"request-supported","claims":[{"claim":"A device is not fully owned when its maker can disable features after sale.","request_basis":"a device is not fully owned when its maker can disable features after sale"}]},{"text":"That may sound like a narrow dispute about software, but it goes to the basic meaning of ownership.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"When we buy something, we expect to decide how it works, when it works, and whether it remains useful after the transaction is over.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"If the maker retains a switch that can turn capabilities off, the buyer has received possession without receiving complete control.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]} ]},{"sentences":[{"text":"The usual defense is that the hardware still sits in the buyer's home (the screen, the battery, the sensors, the casing), so ownership must be intact.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"That argument treats the device as a pile of parts rather than as the thing people actually purchased.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"A modern device is the hardware and the functions that make the hardware useful—and those functions can be withheld even after the money has changed hands.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"The distinction matters because a locked feature is not merely an inconvenience; it is a condition imposed on the buyer's continued use.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]} ]},{"sentences":[{"text":"What exactly has been bought if the most important capabilities remain subject to someone else's permission?","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"The answer cannot simply be that the buyer accepted the terms, because consent to a contract does not erase the difference between owning a tool and renting access to it.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"A person may agree to restrictions, but that agreement should not transform a sale into ownership in name only.","basis":"normative","claims":[]},{"text":"The maker's control is the point—not a technical footnote attached after the fact.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]} ]},{"sentences":[{"text":"This is especially troubling when the disabled feature was part of the reason the device was purchased in the first place.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"The buyer may have paid for a capability, built routines around it, and relied on it as part of the device's identity.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"If that capability can later disappear, the buyer carries the cost while the maker keeps the authority to redefine the product.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"That is less like buying a machine than receiving a key to a machine whose owner can change the lock.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]} ]},{"sentences":[{"text":"The problem is not solved by calling the disabled feature an update, a service decision, or a change to the user experience.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"Those labels describe the maker's action, but they do not answer the ownership question.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"A feature does not become less central because it is delivered through code, and control does not become less real because it is exercised remotely.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"The software layer is still part of the product's practical operation—even if the sales language tries to place it somewhere else.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]} ]},{"sentences":[{"text":"We should be careful about accepting a market where ownership ends at the moment a device leaves the store.","basis":"normative","claims":[]},{"text":"That arrangement gives makers an ongoing veto over products they have already sold, while buyers are left with the bill and a shrinking set of choices.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"It may also encourage companies to design devices around dependency, because a customer who cannot preserve a purchased function is easier to convert into a continuing subscriber.","basis":"hypothetical","claims":[]},{"text":"The result is a marketplace that looks competitive on the shelf but behaves like a series of private permissions afterward.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]} ]},{"sentences":[{"text":"Digital rights have always required us to look past the physical object and ask who actually controls it.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"That question is now unavoidable for ordinary devices, not just for specialized software or online services.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]},{"text":"If a maker can disable features after sale, the buyer should have meaningful rights to keep using what was purchased.","basis":"request-supported","claims":[{"claim":"A maker can disable features after sale.","request_basis":"when its maker can disable features after sale"}]},{"text":"Otherwise, the transaction transfers possession but withholds the authority that ownership is supposed to provide.","basis":"reasoning","claims":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"We should not let a company sell a device as a finished product and reserve the power to make it unfinished later.","basis":"normative","claims":[]},{"text":"A sale should mean more than temporary access dressed up as ownership.","basis":"normative","claims":[]},{"text":"When the maker can reach into a buyer's device and remove what made it worth buying, the buyer owns the object only in the thinnest sense.","basis":"request-supported","claims":[{"claim":"The maker can disable features after sale and thereby remove capabilities from the buyer's device.","request_basis":"when its maker can disable features after sale"}]},{"text":"That is not full ownership, and policy should treat it accordingly.","basis":"normative","claims":[]}]}],"omitted":[{"habit":"opponents-allies-sources / o11: inline hyperlinks and primary-text quotations","why":"The request supplies no verified sources or quotations for this topic."}],"refused":""}
